title: A Lifesaver for the Organised Mind
body:
As someone who thrives on organization and efficiency, I've found Any.do to be an indispensable tool in my daily life. The app's intuitive design and user-friendly interface make task management not just manageable, but actually enjoyable.

Synchronisation Across Devices: One of the standout features of Any.do is its seamless synchronization across all devices. Whether I'm on my phone, tablet, or computer, I can access my tasks and schedules in real-time, ensuring I never miss a beat.

Task Management:The app's task management system is top-notch, with the ability to categorize tasks, set reminders, and even delegate to others. It's like having a personal assistant in your pocket.

Calendar Integration: The integration with the calendar is a game-changer. Being able to view my tasks and appointments in one place helps me plan my day with precision and prevents any scheduling conflicts.

Voice Entry and Widgets:The voice entry feature and the widgets for quick access to my to-do list are incredibly convenient, especially when I'm on the go and need to capture a task quickly.

In conclusion, Any.do has significantly improved my productivity and has helped me stay on top of my busy schedule. It's more than just an app; it's a productivity companion that I highly recommend to anyone looking to streamline their life.

title: Using it for 4 years on and off
body:
I’ve been using Any.do literally from the day it was launched. Honestly, used it on and off. I would always come back to it because of its way of presenting tasks and the innovative and authoritative tasks UI in the GTD approach. 

I always stop using it after a while, ironically, because it has the calendar feature and it does a damn poor job of it. Initially juggling calendar and tasks was hard when any.do lacked this feature. But when it added, I quickly realised how disparate and unimaginative the integration / UI is. Please make the calendar UI “cleaner”.

Lastly, one personal request: kindly use more of the screen real estate by using swiping gestures and hiding the crap tonne of buttons and menus you have always in every screen. I know that it’s one click. But, there are many ways to do one click access to text input and actions without feeling like components have been “slapped” on. 

Someone desperately needs to look at and regain the core strength of any.do - unifying great design with deep understanding of workflow UX.

title: Nice, but could be better
body:
Ok, so the “Plan my day” option is perhaps the best feature of this app that I haven’t seen in any other productivity app. Not even on Evernote. I generally get drained looking at all the tasks I couldn’t complete vs all those I did, and this feature makes that guilt go away with a very simple reschedule that requires minimal effort. This feature is simply too cool. It’s the only reason I subscribed. It even allows syncing with apple reminders which is rather useful.

Now for the cons. The calendar view is annoying as a slight scroll takes me many days ahead or behind. I wish it segregated events and tasks so I could view all my events for the day in one shot rather than scrolling. Also, all my apple reminders gets clubbed in one category here which I honestly find a bit annoying since the colour codes of my lists get lost. I prefer apple reminders as I can add photos to tasks, but this app does not have that feature. (Although it does allow adding notes, subtasks and color coded labels.) For so many missing features, not sure if a subscription fee that is more expensive than an Apple Music subscription is worth it. 

If the developers can look into enhancing the app’s features, I certainly don’t mind spending.

Update for developers as on 2 Mar 2020: Thanks for your quick response! I have updated my rating accordingly. My request was actually for segregating the calendar and tasks in the daily view so I can see all events at one go and then all tasks, without having to scroll. The widget offers me this so it’s a workaround, but would be nice if the app did. And happy to know I can add photos. But I meant adding it to a task directly via the photo itself. Or even add a weblink via the browser. That feature would be so awesome.
